body.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\) under which \(X\) is degenerate, the derivative of the augmented normalized moment map \((S,T_1,\ldots,T_K)\), with \(S=P(A,Z)\) and \(T_u=E\{h_{0,u}(Y)e_Ae_Z^{\mathsf T}\}\), has a right inverse on its observed finite-feature score image whose operator norm is bounded by \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}\).  Applying the corrected \(\mathfrak I_0\) recovers centered derivatives, and hence centered scores, for \(\pi\), \(M_A\), \(M_Z\), and \(\Gamma_Y\) under the modal labeling.
body.justification: This finite-dimensional derivative inversion is the mandatory first gate before any measurable conditional-\(X\) or full-density lifting claim.
body.gap: Allman, Matias, and Rhodes prove level uniqueness of discrete factors, while Hu and Schennach prove full-law recovery through operators; neither result states this quantitative right inverse for the finite normalized tensor derivative.
body.consumer: It provides the constant-covariate kill test and the local inverse needed to begin the full tangent-completeness proof.
body.proof_tex:
Because \(X\) is degenerate, suppress it.  Put \(A_0=M_A\), \(Z_0=M_Z\), \(\Pi=\operatorname{diag}(\pi)\), and let \(\gamma_u^{\mathsf T}\) be row \(u\) of \(\Gamma_Y\).  Three-view independence gives the normalized moment factorizations
\[
 S=A_0\Pi Z_0^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 T_u=A_0\Pi\operatorname{diag}(\gamma_u)Z_0^{\mathsf T}. \tag{6}
\]
Consider a derivative \((\dot\pi,\dot A_0,\dot Z_0,\dot\Gamma)\) in the normalized tangent coordinates, so
\[
 \mathbf 1_K^{\mathsf T}\dot\pi=0,qquad
 \mathbf 1_K^{\mathsf T}\dot A_0=0,qquad
 \mathbf 1_K^{\mathsf T}\dot Z_0=0. \tag{7}
\]
We first prove injectivity of the derivative of (6).  Suppose \(\dot S=0\) and \(\dot T_u=0\) for every \(u\).  Define
\[
 E_A=A_0^{-1}\dot A_0,\qquad E_Z=Z_0^{-1}\dot Z_0,
 \qquad p_j=\dot\pi_j/\pi_j. \tag{8}
\]
Left-multiplying \(\dot S=0\) by \(A_0^{-1}\), right-multiplying by \(Z_0^{-\mathsf T}\), and taking entry \((r,s)\), \(r\ne s\), yields
\[
 (E_A)_{rs}\pi_s+\pi_r(E_Z)_{sr}=0. \tag{9}
\]
The same transformations applied to \(\dot T_u=0\), followed by subtraction of \(\gamma_{ur}\) times (9), give
\[
 (E_A)_{rs}\pi_s(\gamma_{us}-\gamma_{ur})=0,
 \qquad u=1,\ldots,K. \tag{10}
\]
The outcome-feature rank assumption implies
\[
 \|\gamma_s-\gamma_r\|_2
 =\|\Gamma_Y(e_s-e_r)\|_2
 \geq\varepsilon\|e_s-e_r\|_2=\sqrt 2\,\varepsilon. \tag{11}
\]
Together with \(\pi_s\geq\varepsilon\), equations (10)--(11) imply \((E_A)_{rs}=0\); equation (9) then implies \((E_Z)_{sr}=0\).  Hence \(E_A\) and \(E_Z\) are diagonal.  Since \(\mathbf 1_K^{\mathsf T}A_0=\mathbf 1_K^{\mathsf T}\), (7)--(8) give \(\mathbf 1_K^{\mathsf T}E_A=0\), so the diagonal matrix \(E_A\) is zero.  Similarly \(E_Z=0\).  The diagonal entries of the transformed equation \(\dot S=0\) now give \(\dot\pi=0\), and those of every transformed equation \(\dot T_u=0\) give \(\dot\gamma_{ur}=0\) for all \(u,r\).  Thus the derivative is injective on the normalized tangent space.

The admissible finite tuples lie in a compact set: the stochastic columns and \(\pi\) lie in finite products of compact simplices; the three least-singular-value restrictions and the propensity lower bound define closed subsets; and \(|\Gamma_{Y,uj}|\leq\|h_0\|_\infty\).  The derivative matrix in (6) depends continuously on this tuple.  Its least singular value on the normalized tangent space is positive pointwise by the preceding injectivity argument.  If its infimum on the compact set were zero, a convergent minimizing subsequence and continuity would produce a tuple with a nontrivial null vector, contradicting injectivity.  Hence the infimum is a positive constant depending only on \(K,\varepsilon\), and \(\|h_0\|_\infty\).  Its Moore--Penrose right inverse on the image is therefore bounded by \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}\), after enlarging that declared constant if necessary.

On a fixed-rank finite-dimensional set, the Moore--Penrose inverse is a Borel function: locally one may select a nonzero maximal minor, write the inverse on that chart by ratios of determinants, and cover the set by finitely many such charts.  Theorem 1 supplies the identified common permutation, while the modal gap makes its ordered choice locally constant.  Thus applying this Borel inverse to the differentiated observed moments measurably recovers the normalized derivatives under the ordered labeling.  At a positive categorical atom, its factor score is derivative divided by the atom probability.  At a zero atom, nonnegativity of a two-sided probability path forces its derivative to be zero, so assigning score zero is valid.  Equations (7) then give factorwise centering.  This is the asserted bounded right inverse on the observed finite-feature score image.
